provenance.construction: Reversing fold of a pair-partition CPM CSS code with J = 4, L = 12, P = 113. Parent qubit q = c*P + t. Parent X row (j,s) meets c*P + ((s - E[j][c]) mod P) for each block c. The involution is pi(c*P + t) = sigma[c]*P + ((-t - B[sigma[c]]) mod P). Folded site pairs (c, t) for c < sigma[c] with its image under pi; each parent X row becomes one stabilizer generator, X on representatives and Z on partners. E = [[97, 112, 42, 112, 16, 6, 91, 42, 76, 105, 40, 24], [33, 84, 44, 64, 21, 19, 17, 68, 12, 8, 25, 109], [63, 106, 64, 12, 87, 47, 108, 85, 101, 25, 6, 93], [14, 106, 74, 73, 79, 67, 80, 46, 103, 22, 31, 21]], sigma = [11, 6, 8, 7, 9, 10, 1, 3, 2, 4, 5, 0], B = [68, 65, 18, 42, 101, 34, 65, 42, 18, 101, 34, 68].
provenance.notes: Discovered by lifting the (J,L)=(4,12) reversing-fold CPM pair-partition linear system to prime P=113 (zero cyclic subcodes). Tightened via 325,000+ C++ symplectic Stern ISD trials (15x3,000 4-block + 6x2,500 5-block + 175,000 block-biased + 90,000 uniform). Distance revision 2026-11-26 (witness by @FarLab): P side 80 -> 22 (CPU random-information-set search (verify/gf2_fast.cpp, distance_rand_witness, pair depth 32), 144,487 trials per side, seed 1533682674).
